item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00350","case1_error":"Uses purchase cost per egg instead of the stated selling price to calculate capital recovery.","case2_error":"Invents a $1 coin value and treats the three coins sold as the initial coin count.","reason":"The first substitutes the wrong price; the second invents a denomination and misassigns a quantity, independently of the ambiguous $12 wording.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00351","case1_error":"Omits the factor of two in each two-dozen set, calculating 48 cups instead of 96.","case2_error":"Omits the factor of nine people, calculating pages for only one person's copies.","reason":"Both omit a required multiplicative factor when aggregating quantities across groups.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J00352","case1_error":"Omits the $20 flat fee from the total deposit.","case2_error":"Evaluates the correctly written sum 132 + 35 as 144 instead of 167.","reason":"The first leaves out a required charge; the second numerically miscalculates a correct expression.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00353","case1_error":"Uses one bottle's 80-load capacity as the total capacity for two bottles.","case2_error":"Ignores the additional 20% bulk discount when calculating savings.","reason":"The first fails to scale capacity by bottle count; the second omits a separate percentage discount.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00354","case1_error":"Counts the two mother lambs again despite their inclusion in the original six.","case2_error":"Evaluates 8 + 12 + 16 + 4 as 30 instead of 40.","reason":"The first double-counts members of an existing total; the second miscalculates a correctly constructed sum.","judgment":"different"}]}
